mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (rising from -43.3% to -36.1% over four weeks) reflects a consistent recovery trend that will continue linearly over the next four weeks, producing higher mean RETAIL_REC in the forward period than the backward period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 7.2 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -31.7% to -25.3% (6.4 point improvement), signaling return of commuting behavior. This restores weekday retail foot traffic patterns and social shopping routines, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves more than 5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean when WORKPLACES continues to improve.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered sharply from -50.3% to -20.6% (29.7 point gain), indicating outdoor activity resumption. This substitutes for indoor retail-and-recreation, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks despite overall mobility recovery.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves more than 25 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28-day mean when PARKS continues to improve.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent recovery in both WORKPLACES (up 6.4 points) and PARKS (up 29.7 points) creates a bifurcated mobility pattern: commuters return but divert leisure time to outdoor spaces. The net effect on RETAIL_REC depends on whether workplace-driven weekday retail gains exceed outdoor-substitution losses. Interaction of these two proxies determines the direction.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and PARKS improve simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improvement (29.7 points) exceeds WORKPLACES improvement (6.4 points)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28-day mean when both WORKPLACES and PARKS improve and PARKS gain exceeds WORKPLACES gain.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has recovered from -43.3% to -37.1% (6.2 point improvement), indicating increased public transportation use. This enables retail-and-recreation access for transit-dependent populations, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks as the effect manifests quickly.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves more than 5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not show improvement relative to the prior 14-day mean when TRANSIT continues to improve.

candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 12% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28-day mean when RESIDENTIAL continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near -5.7% (minimal change from -12.0%), indicating essential-goods shopping is normalized. When essential-goods access is assured, consumers redirect discretionary spending to retail-and-recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM changed only 1.4 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28-day mean when GROCERY_PHARM remains stable.
